text:
Abstract
We queried NCBI GEO for Escherichia coli expression studies involving ciprofloxacin using the GEO Series filter. The structured search returned 37 matching Series records (term: "Escherichia coli" AND ciprofloxacin, entry_type=gse), with the service noting MeSH-based query translation and response truncation. We then retrieved detailed Series metadata and supplementary file listings for three ciprofloxacin-relevant E. coli RNA-seq studies: GSE295494 (time-resolved exposure; 42 samples), GSE292923 (ΔpurA tolerance during ciprofloxacin; 4 samples), and GSE275261 (includes E. coli ciprofloxacin treatment; 24 samples). Linked PubMed records were summarized for five PMIDs associated with these Series and related datasets. Key numbers: total Series matching term=37; detailed Series examined=3; sample counts=42, 4, and 24; all three provide downloadable processed matrices via GEO FTP. These results show that E. coli expression datasets addressing ciprofloxacin exposure exist in GEO, spanning immediate transcriptional responses, genetic determinants of tolerance, and comparative antibiotic modes of action. This matters for antibiotic response modeling, resistance/tolerance mechanism discovery, and reproducible reanalysis because GEO hosts processed matrices necessary for downstream computational workflows.

I. Introduction
Background. Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic targeting bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. Understanding E. coli transcriptomic responses to ciprofloxacin informs mechanisms of stress adaptation, tolerance, and resistance, and supports the development of adjuvants or new antibiotics.
Literature Review. We retrieved PubMed summaries linked to the GEO Series: mSystems (PMID 41805196) on early antibiotic exposure; mLife (PMID 42079445) on quinolone tolerance via adenylosuccinate synthetase defects; J Bacteriol (PMID 39235234) comparing GuaB inhibition with ciprofloxacin; Nature (PMID 40804527) on E. coli genome organization includes datasets with ciprofloxacin perturbations; mSphere (PMID 40879398) on an antimicrobial peptide reducing resistance to ciprofloxacin. No literature was retrieved for GSE309890.
Knowledge Gap. Whether GEO holds E. coli expression datasets explicitly involving ciprofloxacin, and which records provide processed matrices for reanalysis.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Identify E. coli expression studies in GEO that investigate ciprofloxacin. Hypothesis: GEO contains multiple RNA-seq Series with ciprofloxacin exposure and downloadable processed data.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We used NCBI GEO to identify expression Series (GSE) for Escherichia coli with ciprofloxacin in the record text, then inspected selected Series for detailed metadata and supplementary processed matrices. We summarized linked PubMed citations for context.
Materials.
- NCBI GEO via geo_search and geo_series.
- PubMed via pubmed_get_summaries.
Procedures.
- geo_search with arguments: organism="Escherichia coli", term="ciprofloxacin", entry_type="gse", max_results=20. The tool returned query translation and counts.
- pubmed_get_summaries with pmids=["40879398","40804527","41805196","42079445","39235234"] to summarize citations linked to selected Series.
- geo_series for detailed records and files:
  • accession="GSE295494", list_files=true.
  • accession="GSE292923", list_files=true.
  • accession="GSE275261", list_files=true.
Statistical Analysis.
- The 37 Series count came from geo_search.total_count.
- We reported sample_count, platform, and date_public directly from geo_series fields for each accession.
- No deduplication was required; each accession is unique.
- Literature counts reflect the exact PMIDs returned; no percentages were computed.

III. Results
Data Presentation. Table 1. E. coli GEO Series with ciprofloxacin exposure examined in detail.

| Accession | Title | Date public | Organism | Experiment type | Sample count | Platform | PubMed PMID(s) | FTP directory |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSE295494 | Revealing Transcriptomic Responses in Escherichia coli During Early Antibiotic Exposure | 2025/05/01 | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | 42 | GPL26592 | 41805196 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE295nnn/GSE295494/ |
| GSE292923 | RNA-seq analyzes the effect of purA on transcriptome in Escherichia coli during ciprofloxacin treatment. | 2025/03/25 | Escherichia coli | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | 4 | GPL18133 | 42079445 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE292nnn/GSE292923/ |
| GSE275261 | Differential effects of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH/GuaB) inhibition in Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli | 2024/08/25 | Acinetobacter baumannii; Escherichia coli | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | 24 | GPL22143;21433 | 39235234 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE275nnn/GSE275261/ |

Findings.
- The GEO search returned 37 Series records matching the organism and ciprofloxacin term.
- Detailed inspection confirmed at least three RNA-seq Series directly involving E. coli ciprofloxacin exposure with processed matrices available via FTP.
- Supplementary files are present:
  • GSE295494: raw_counts.csv.gz (size 298K).
  • GSE292923: four differential expression TXT matrices.
  • GSE275261: species-specific counts and metadata TXT files.
- PubMed links exist for 4 of the 3 examined Series and one related dataset (total PMIDs summarized: 5).

IV. Discussion
Interpretation.
- GEO contains multiple E. coli expression studies involving ciprofloxacin; three examined Series provide RNA-seq data with accessible processed matrices. This meets the objective, establishing that such datasets are available for reanalysis.
Context.
- The mSystems study (PMID 41805196) corresponds to GSE295494 time-resolved ciprofloxacin exposure. The mLife study (PMID 42079445) aligns with GSE292923’s ΔpurA model under ciprofloxacin. J Bacteriol (PMID 39235234) includes E. coli ciprofloxacin exposure alongside GuaB inhibition in GSE275261. The Nature study (PMID 40804527) includes datasets with ciprofloxacin perturbations in a broader genomic architecture context.
Limitations.
- The GEO search response was truncated; only a subset of records was returned. NCBI’s query translation via MeSH may broaden/narrow matches relative to the raw term. GEO’s API returns metadata only; processed expression values must be downloaded from the FTP directories listed. PubMed summaries reflect linked records; absence of a PubMed link in GEO does not imply lack of data.
Conclusion & Future Directions.
- Yes: E. coli expression studies about ciprofloxacin exist in GEO; three RNA-seq Series were identified with downloadable matrices. Next steps: expand geo_series retrieval to additional accessions from the 37 counted records; optionally generate a downloadable TSV listing all matched GSEs and their FTP file URLs; perform standardized reanalysis.

[7] GSE292923 supplementary files: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE292nnn/GSE292923/suppl/
[8] GEO Series GSE275261 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE275261
[9] GSE275261 FTP directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE275nnn/GSE275261/
[10] GSE275261 supplementary files: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE275nnn/GSE275261/suppl/
[11] PubMed summary for PMID 41805196: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41805196/
